identity.title: Engineering split activators for controlled-background CRISPR/Cas12a molecular logic biosensing of AFB1 and OTA.

content.abstract: Mycotoxin co-occurrence of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) and ochratoxin A (OTA) in dairy products threatens food safety. Conventional methods suffer from complex procedures and limited multi-target analysis. Current CRISPR/Cas12a sensors face nonspecific background and poor programmability. We developed a CRISPR/Cas12a logic gate biosensing platform with split DNA activators, enabling individual AFB1 and OTA quantification via dual YES gates and logic-based qualitative multi-target analysis via OR, AND, INHIBIT, and NOR gates. Integrating aptamer recognition, target-triggered strand displacement amplification (SDA), and Cas12a trans-cleavage, the split activators reduced nonspecific activation, enabling low background for target-dependent logic gates. YES, OR, AND, INHIBIT, and NOR gates were constructed. Linear ranges were 0.1-500 ng/mL for OTA and 0.05-500 ng/mL for AFB1, with detection limits of 0.0755 and 0.0381 ng/mL, respectively. The platform showed good selectivity and satisfactory recoveries in spiked pretreated milk. This work provides a programmable, low-background strategy for CRISPR-based multi-mycotoxin analysis in pretreated milk matrices.
